# disktree 0.11.0

A release of the **fork** at
[SteMoeller/disktree](https://github.com/SteMoeller/disktree), built on top of
upstream [tobi/disktree](https://github.com/tobi/disktree). It carries the whole
DISK ticket series — developed on Windows 11 with a self-written AI ticketing
helper — **and** everything merged in from upstream since the fork.

## Added and changed in this fork (DISK series)

### Interface, language and zoom

- **DISK-3 — Volume list, zoom and language (i18n).** The bottom bar gained a
  volume picker (`v`), interface zoom (`ctrl` `+`/`-`/`0`) and a language
  picker; the strings moved into `disktree.<lang>.i18n.txt`, looked up beside
  the executable, in the working directory, then under `%APPDATA%\disktree`.
- **DISK-5 — Missing i18n keys.** The bottom-menu labels are looked up through
  `t(variable)`; the capitalised-only entries left `mark`, `open`, `up` and
  friends English. The indirect keys are covered now.
- **DISK-7 — System language.** A German Windows starts in German; the picker
  still overrides it.
- **DISK-8 / DISK-14 — Hover help.** Every bottom-bar command has a hover help
  in English and German, and “move” now names the arrow keys as well as `hjkl`.

### Treemap and rendering

- **DISK-4 — Raised blocks and file-type colours.** Optional raised 3D tiles and
  colours per file extension from `disktree.ext.colors.txt`, switchable in the
  legend row; a directory takes the colour of the extension holding the most
  bytes beneath it.
- **DISK-13 — Eight block styles.** A dropdown picks between eight ways to draw
  a raised tile, each derived from the tile’s own colour, with *Classic* the
  flat default; the label band reserves a style’s inner ring, and *Gloss* keeps
  the base colour instead of washing it grey.
- **DISK-10 — Copy path.** A right-click on a tile copies its full path.

### Cloud / OneDrive

- **DISK-11 — Cloud placeholder audit.** Online-only folders are recognised and
  skipped, but a file’s `RECALL_ON_*` attribute was read and then ignored; this
  is the basis for DISK-15.
- **DISK-15 — Cloud space.** Dehydrated files are evaluated per file, and the
  space held only in the cloud is carried as its own number beside the local
  allocation. The selection panel shows a distinct “In the cloud” value for
  files and directories alike, and nothing is hydrated.

### Volumes, window and admin

- **DISK-12 — Mapped drives in an admin run.** An elevated process has its own
  logon session, so `GetLogicalDrives` lost the user’s mapped letters and the
  picker showed only local disks; it now reconnects the remembered
  `HKCU\Network` mappings for that process.
- **DISK-16 — Sorted volume picker.** Volumes list by name (drive letter), and
  the volume being scanned carries a coloured outline.
- **DISK-6 — Start monitor.** The window opens centred on the monitor disktree
  was launched from (visible console → foreground window → pointer); gpui is
  also told the display, or it snaps the window to the primary.
- **DISK-17 — Faster admin start.** `-A`/`--administrator` elevates before any
  scan begins, and `ctrl-shift-a` restarts as administrator from the first
  frame instead of waiting for the walk to report errors.

### Windows, repo and docs

- **DISK-2 — Windows build script.** `build.ps1` takes a fresh checkout to
  `target\release\disktree.exe`, importing the MSVC environment and installing
  Rust into a repo-local `.tools\` when it cannot go system-wide.
- **DISK-9 — Feature branch.** The ticket work lands on `feature/disk-series`,
  one commit per ticket with English messages.
- **DISK-1 — Security audit.** A read-only review: no telemetry, update checks
  or HTTP; the first-party code does not leave the machine.
- **DISK-18 — README.** The Windows 11 series and every ticket are documented.
- Also: the `LICENSE` credits the fork author, `.tickets/` is tracked, and the
  file-type colour files ship with a slimmed example plus the full set.

## Merged from upstream `tobi/disktree`

- **PR #46** — cocoon fix.
- **PR #52** — flag a marked path whose name is not valid Unicode.
- **PR #63** — bound scan admission and adapt worker budgets:
  - `perf: bound scan admission and adapt macOS worker budgets`
  - `perf: retain direct Rayon dispatch for pool-sized fixed scans`
  - `fix: allow platform-specific CPU sampler fallback lints`
- **Power Efficiency** in the settings row: saved worker presets, a gauge, a
  corrected tradeoff tooltip, and a benchmark behind it
  (`feat: add saved Power Efficiency scan worker presets`,
  `feat: show Power Efficiency as a gauge in the settings row`,
  `fix: state the measured Power Efficiency tradeoff in the tooltip`,
  `fix: keep a check on the saved Power Efficiency preset`,
  `chore: add the scan-worker benchmark behind the Power Efficiency table`).
- **README**: the `t` key cycles three modes, not two.

## Install

Download the archive for your platform below and unpack it: run `install.sh`
on Linux, or `disktree.exe` on Windows. On macOS, unzip and drag
`disktree.app` into Applications; the build is signed ad hoc, so clear the
quarantine mark once if Gatekeeper objects:

```sh
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/disktree.app
```
